summary.en: Israel is intensifying airstrikes and artillery against Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon, while Hezbollah monitors Israeli naval forces from Lebanese fishing boats. The Lebanese prime minister says a proposal is under way to keep UNIFIL operating beyond the end of the year to avoid a security vacuum as the force prepares to withdraw. Lebanon fears Israel may impose a maritime buffer zone in its southern waters, and France is planning a phased withdrawal of international forces after UNIFIL leaves. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel intensiverer luftangrep og artilleri mot Hizbollah-posisjoner i Sør-Libanon, mens Hizbollah overvåker israelske marinekrefter fra libanesiske fiskebåter. Den libanesiske statsministeren sier at et forslag er under arbeid for å holde FN-styrken i Libanon (UNIFIL) i drift utover årsskiftet for å unngå et sikkerhetsvakuum når styrken forbereder seg på å trekke seg tilbake. Libanon frykter at Israel kan innføre en maritim buffer­soner i deres sørlige farvann, og Frankrike planlegger en trinnvis tilbaketrekning av internasjonale styrker etter at UNIFIL forlater området. Konflikten har forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
